sourcing.title: How we source
sourcing.body: Dates are shown as scholarly ranges, not single years. Each claim carries citations, a confidence level, and a review status. Claims in this build are self-reviewed, not scholar-approved — a qualified historical geographer has not yet signed them off, and a store release is blocked until that happens. Tertiary sources — Wikipedia, popular encyclopedias, study-Bible maps, devotional sites — are only ever orienting links, never the sole authority: every claim is also backed by a concrete source (a primary text, a standard scholarly work, an excavation report, or a gazetteer), and the content build blocks any claim that rests on tertiary sources alone. High-confidence coordinates must additionally carry a place-specific citation or a Pleiades gazetteer id — a whole-atlas reference is not enough. Ambiguous locations draw every rival candidate as a hollow marker and list them in the site panel, rather than implying a single pin. Route strokes are drawn by geometry grade so a surveyed Roman road never looks like a schematic connector. Where scholars or traditions disagree, we say so. Bible text is public domain (King James Version, American Standard Version). This atlas is carefully cited and reviewed — it does not claim to be definitive.

candidates.title: Rival identifications
candidates.intro: Scholars do not agree on a single pin. The filled marker is the working identification; hollow markers on the map are the documented rivals.
